To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA binding domain of a steroid hormone receptor is composed of a minimal zinc finger core and a contiguous C-terminal domain, and that the C-terminal domain contains overlapping, but separable, determinants of DNA and nuclear localization.
a mutation in a region near the DAF- 12 DBD C terminus, but outside the minimal DBD core, dramatically decreases DNA binding affinity and transcriptional regulatory activity.

the C-terminal region of the DAF-2 DBD is important for both nuclear localization and DNA binding, and that the C-terminal end of the DBD contains overlapping but separable DNA binding and nuclear targeting sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel and unexpected role of the C-terminal end of a zinc finger DNA binding motif, which is conserved in the DAF-2/DAF-16 and DAF-12 orthologs in Drosophila and humans.
the role of a conserved arginine in the C-terminal region of the DAF-2 DBD, and how this arginine contributes to DNA binding and nuclear import.
the molecular basis of the DAF- 12 transcriptional regulatory mechanism, and we have identified a region in which the determinants of DNA recognition and nuclear localization are tightly coupled.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Arg197 is required for DNA binding but is not required for nuclear localization.

Arg197 and the adjacent three basic residues are critical for DAF-12 activity, and that the C-terminal region of the DAF- 12 DNA binding domain contains separable determinants that are required for both DNA binding and nuclear import.
the DAF-2 DBD C-terminal domain contains overlapping but separable nuclear localization and DNA binding determinants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DAF- 12 DBD C-terminus is important for both DNA binding and nuclear targeting, and that the latter activity is not required for the former.
the DAF- 12 DBD C terminus is important for DNA binding and nuclear targeting and that the C-terminal residues of DAF-12 and other nuclear receptors can play a role in both of these processes.
the C-terminal region of the DAF-2 DBD is important for both DNA binding and nuclear import.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DAF-2/DAF-16/DAF-12 pathway, which controls longevity, stress resistance and metabolism, is a prime target for drug discovery.
the DAF-2/DAF-16/DAF-12 signaling axis, a major regulator of longevity in worms and flies, is a promising new target for the development of antiaging drugs.
the DAF-2/DAF-16 and DAF-2/DAP-16 pathways are not the only pathways that are important for the regulation of lifespan.
